items.name: v0.34.0
items.body:
# v0.34.0

**1,061 commits from 412 contributors (120 new).** Thank you!

## TL;DR

- **10 new models** (Mistral Large 4, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe, and more!)
- **Extensible KV cache is on by default:** vLLM sizes the KV cache from memory actually free after warmup, so most models get a bigger cache and more throughput.
- **Model Runner V1 is gone.** Model Runner V2 is now the only GPU runner.
- **Big speedups** on Blackwell and MI355X: up to 1.95× decode (Step5 on GB200), 1.6× throughput (GLM-5.3-Flash), 1.24–1.40× faster long-prompt TTFT (GLM-5.3).
- **Upgrade check:** default block size is now 64, ROCm 7.2 images are gone, and `huggingface_hub >= 2.0.0` is required. See [Before you upgrade](#before-you-upgrade).

## Before you upgrade

> [!IMPORTANT]
> These changes can break existing setups.

| Change | What to do | PR |
|---|---|---|
| Model Runner V1 removed | Remove `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`; it now fails at startup. Port V1 logits processors to `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor`. | #63373 |
| Default `--block-size` is 64 (was 16) | Pass `--block-size 16` to keep the old behavior. ROCm paged attention still uses 16. | #63231 |
| Extensible KV cache on by default; `gpu_memory_utilization` defaults to 1.0 | To keep the old sizing, pass `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` or `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`. | #56492 |
| ROCm 7.2 artifacts dropped | Use the ROCm 10.0 wheels and images. `-rocm72` is no longer published. | #61939 |
| `huggingface_hub >= 2.0.0` required | Also requires `tokenizers >= 0.23.3` and `timm >= 1.0.30`. | #64779 |
| QuTLASS / `fp_quant` removed | `fp_quant` checkpoints no longer load. | #65230 |
| Marlin W4A8 removed | Use `--quantization humming` with `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` instead of `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT

items.body:
<details open>

ui: move the web UI to ui/apps/chat and call it Llama Chat (#32032)

* ui: move tools/ui to ui/apps/chat

The chat app moves to its own root folder, ui/apps/chat, as the first step of splitting the UI into one library
(ui/lib) and the apps built on it (ui/apps). The code is unchanged; every path that pointed at tools/ui now points at
ui/apps/chat: CMake adds it from tools/, and the Dockerfiles, the Nix package, the workflows, the labeler, CODEOWNERS,
.editorconfig, the git hooks, the dev and demo scripts and the docs follow it.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: name Llama Chat's package @ggml-org/llama-chat

It was still called llama-ui, the name of the library that now sits beside it
in ui/lib (@ggml-org/llama-ui). The package stays private; the app's display name
and the llama-ui.zip build artifact are unchanged.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: call the built-in web UI Llama Chat in docs, help text and comments

The app in tools/ui is Llama Chat; Llama UI is the component library it is
built from. Prose that said "Web UI", "web UI" or "WebUI" for the app now
names it: the READMEs, SECURITY.md, the --ui help text, the CMake option
description, one server log line, code comments and the Storybook intro.

Names that others depend on are unchanged: the deprecated --webui flag
aliases, the LLAMA_*_WEBUI CMake and environment names, the webui_settings
field, the storage migration keys and the Nix attributes.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: name tools/ui as a former path of Llama Chat in the code-review skill

Changes under the old tools/ui path, as well as tools/server/webui, still
get the Llama Chat checklist.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

* ui: name Llama Chat's path in the security policy's exclusions
